clue.text: One with little time by river (one from the North)

parts.note: the Esk is a river in northern England and Scotland
the Roman numeral for one
a mo is a moment, as in 'half a mo'

explanation.surface: Someone short of time standing by a river, glossed in brackets as a northerner.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read back to front: the river comes first, then the one and the little time.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a member of the Arctic peoples of the far north, though many now prefer Inuit.

clue.text: Mark cooked pies with mash

definitions.note: a noun here: a mark of stress

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked on and changed, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook called Mark preparing pies and mash, the classic London meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name or a verb, but it is the noun for stress placed on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress or special importance marked on something, as with an underline or accent.

clue.text: Book about prize flowers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: Kings is a book of the Old Testament
a cup is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: A book about prize-winning flowers, as at a horticultural show.
explanation.walkthrough: The trophy sits inside the name of the Bible book, splitting it after KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingcups are marsh marigolds, yellow-flowered plants of wet ground.

clue.text: Wander about a lot with two ducks instead of you, say

indicators.note: instead of means one thing replaces another in the word

parts.note: much means a lot
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, written O, so two of them
the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: Strolling around with a couple of ducks in place of a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: The U in MUCH is swapped out for the two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to wander aimlessly or loiter about with no particular purpose.

clue.text: Hold for making a cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a wrestling grip made with the legs locked round an opponent
second meaning: a two-bladed cutting tool

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an instruction to keep something still while slicing; the hold is the wrestling move.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wrestling hold with crossed legs and the familiar bladed tool used to cut paper or cloth.

clue.text: Thorough study by eg chemist mainly to include Open University

indicators.note: to include means taking something inside, so letters go within the word
mainly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a chemist is an example of a scientist
the standard abbreviation for the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A careful piece of research by a chemist with Open University involvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg chemist' signals a broader category the chemist belongs to; 'mainly' trims that word before the university's initials go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscientious describes someone careful and diligent, doing work with thoroughness.

clue.text: Badly-designed t-terraces used for kind of tram

indicators.note: something badly designed is put together wrongly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, the stammered T included

explanation.surface: Poorly planned terraced streets laid out for a tramline, with a stutter on the t.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd stutter 't-terraces' supplies the extra T the letters need.
explanation.definitionFit: Streetcar is the North American word for a tram running on rails in the street.

clue.text: "Dream" satellite

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fairy king in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
second meaning: one of the moons of Uranus

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show 'Dream' is short for the play title, so the first definition is a character in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the fairy king in Shakespeare's play, and the outer moon of Uranus bearing the same name.

clue.text: Dog races central to profit, say

indicators.note: central to means sitting in the middle of another word
say means the word before is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: profit sounds like prophet, and a prophet is a seer
the TT races are the Tourist Trophy motorbike races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Dog racing is key to making money, someone claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profit, say' is the sound-alike prophet, which then becomes its synonym SEER, split by the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of gun dog trained to stand still pointing at game.

clue.text: Fix to a horse?

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to attach something to a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or skewbald horse, with patches of white and another colour.

clue.text: Success with sitter curling — when the climate's so?

parts.note: a win is a success

indicators.note: curling means twisting round, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A curling team winning easily, and asking whether the weather is suitably cold for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling is a winter ice sport, which makes the anagram signal fit the surface so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter conditions are at their most extreme when the climate is wintriest, coldest and snowiest.

clue.text: Bill for the very first printing?

definitions.text: Bill for the very first printing?

parts.words: Bill for the very first printing?
parts.note: surface reading: an invoice for a first print run

parts.words: Bill for the very first printing?
parts.note: setter's reading: Bill is short for a man's first name, and he did the first printing in England

explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like an invoice but is the familiar form of a first name; the man in question set up England's first printing press in 1476.
explanation.definitionFit: The man named was the merchant who introduced the printing press to England and printed its first books.

clue.text: One isn't TT, but might be AA

definitions.text: One isn't TT, but might be AA

parts.words: One isn't TT, but might be AA
parts.note: surface reading: not a motorbike race but a motoring organisation, the Automobile Association

parts.words: One isn't TT, but might be AA
parts.note: setter's reading: TT means teetotal

explanation.walkthrough: TT and AA both look like motoring references (the Isle of Man races and the Automobile Association); read as teetotal and Alcoholics Anonymous they describe a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone addicted to drink is not teetotal and may well be a member of the support group for drinkers.

clue.text: European with European backing to run for Union?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: Europeans backing someone running for election in a union.
explanation.walkthrough: Union here means marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly in order to marry.

clue.text: Face nerve in cheek

definitions.meaning: first meaning: brazen boldness, as in 'the face to ask'

explanation.surface: A facial nerve located in the cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: All three anatomical words are separate meanings of rudeness; 'in' merely joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Face, nerve and cheek are all informal words for audacious rudeness or disrespect.

clue.text: Something prepared if mere alp is to be shown up?

definitions.text: Something prepared if mere alp is to be shown up?

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready from raw material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thing made so that even a modest mountain stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, since such a map is made to make high ground stand out.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows hills and mountains in raised form or shading, so heights stand out visibly.

clue.text: Making confession to having property risen in value

parts.note: owning means having something as property
shares that are up have risen

explanation.surface: Someone confessing that their property has gone up in value.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit or confess a fault, so the phrase describes making confession.

clue.text: A retrial in motion, denoting the importance of the route

definitions.text: denoting the importance of the route

indicators.note: in motion means moving about, so the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A legal retrial is under way, and its route is significant.
explanation.definitionFit: An arterial road is a main route, named by comparison with the body's main blood vessels.

clue.text: Weapon made of strong material with propeller

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud or strong
lamé is a fabric woven with metallic thread
one who propels something is a thrower
a joining word

explanation.surface: A weapon built from tough material and fitted with a propeller.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamé is a glittering fabric with metal thread in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamethrower is a weapon projecting a stream of burning fuel.

clue.text: Outlaw musical group's item? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word survives, the rest being dropped

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether an outlaw is part of a band's set, with the cheeky reply 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it cuts ITEM in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber or outlaw, especially one in a gang.

clue.text: Head needs oxygen following a space programme

parts.note: taken as written
poll is an old word for the head
the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An astronaut's head needs oxygen on a space programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the A in front of the head and its oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the NASA programme that landed astronauts on the Moon.

clue.text: Stout piece of material with no fringes

indicators.note: fringes are edges, so without them the outermost letters go

parts.note: a sampler is a piece of embroidered cloth showing off stitches

explanation.surface: A stout bit of cloth that has had its fringed edges trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample, like stout, describes a large or generously proportioned figure.

clue.text: A musical sound item attenuated once

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: attenuated means stretched thin and altered in shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tone is a musical sound
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single musical note being softened and thinned out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attenuated' is an unusual anagram signal, here stretching ITEM out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: At one time means formerly, in the past, just as once does.

clue.text: Tramp (not black) sees moth (brown)

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letter is left out

parts.note: a tramp is a vagrant who begs
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A tramp, described as not dark-skinned, watching a brown moth.
explanation.walkthrough: '(brown)' is part of the definition, describing the colour of the moth.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggars are large brown moths whose caterpillars build egg-shaped cocoons.

clue.text: Smiled too freely in the Italian Alps

indicators.note: freely means without restraint, so the letters are free to fall in any order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A happy holidaymaker grinning widely in the mountains of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dolomites are a range of limestone mountains in north-east Italy, part of the Alpine system.

clue.text: Old singer's engagement by lake (Italy)

parts.note: a gig is a booked performance, an engagement for a musician
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A veteran singer's booking for a concert beside an Italian lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed Italy reads like a location for the lake but supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beniamino Gigli was a celebrated Italian operatic tenor of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Parading porn I got abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone showing off the smut they picked up on a trip overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Trooping means marching in formation, as in Trooping the Colour, a ceremonial parade.

clue.text: Guy in place for launch

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast steady

explanation.surface: A man installed in position for a product launch.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy looks like a man but is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel is to drive or launch something forward.
